5. The captioned appeal has been preferred by the appellant, seeking setting aside of the Judgment and Order on Sentence dated 05th March 2024 and 11th July 2024 respectively, passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-1 (POCSO), North-West, Rohini

The prosecution case, in brief, is that on 29.10.2019, appellant committed aggravated penetrated sexual assault upon victim "K", who was then aged about five years.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the conviction recorded by the learned Trial Court suffers from grave infirmities and there are material contradictions and improvements in This is a digitally signed order.

He further submits that the statement of the victim was recorded after a delay of 16 days, and in such statement, the allegations of penetrative sexual assault is missing.
It is also submitted that the MLC of the victim does not show any external injuries on her private parts and the same is therefore not suggestive of penetrative sexual assault.
It is also stated that in the FSL result, there is no mention of initials of seal.
The police official, who deposited the exhibits at FSL, has not been examined, and therefore, the crucial link evidence is missing.

It is further submitted that appellant has undergone incarceration of about six years and there is no likelihood of appeal being heard in near future.
8.
The learned APP, who appears for the State, submits that the victim and her mother have duly supported the prosecution case.

He states that when the victim had gone to toilet, the appellant caught hold of her and gave beatings to her and bit her on her cheeks with his teeth, injured her left eye and cheek and committed penetrative intercourse with her and when she raised alarm, her mother came there searching her and found that victim had no clothes on her body and was having Ashraf Rain vs The State (Govt. The FSL result confirms the presence of appellant's DNA on the Pajami and underwear of the victim.

9. It is trite that suspension of sentence under Section 389 of the Cr.P.C (now, section 430, BNSS) is not a matter of right.
The nature, gravity and impact of the offence on the victim and society are vital considerations.

The Supreme Court in Shivani Tyagi v. State of U.P. & Anr., 2024 SCC OnLine SC 842, held that sentence cannot be suspended merely on the ground of incarceration or delay in appeal process, but the same has to be decided on its own merits.

sentences.text: 10. The learned Trial Court in the impugned judgment has recorded detailed findings after appreciation of evidence and came to the conclusion that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.

11. At this stage, this Court is not inclined to undertake re- appreciation of evidence or examine the correctness of the findings recorded by the Trial Court, as any observation at this stage may prejudice the appellant.
The only consideration, before this Court at this stage, is as to whether the appellant has made out any ground for suspension or not.
The pleas raised are the matters to be considered at the final hearing of the appeal.
12. Having been convicted, the presumption of innocence is no more available to the appellant.
No exceptional or compelling circumstances have been brought to the fore that would warrant suspension of sentence at this stage.
Merely because the appellant has undergone incarceration for a period of about six years, shall not This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/02/2026 at 20:36:20 constitute any ground for grant of suspension of sentence, particularly, in view of the grave nature of the offence.
13. In view of the foregoing and considering the seriousness of offence and overall facts and evidence, we do not deem it appropriate to suspend the sentence of the appellant at this stage.

14. It is clarified that any observations made herein are purely for the purpose of deciding the question of suspension of sentence and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
